label: Place
name: South Korea
summary:
South Korea, officially the Republic of Korea (ROK), is a country in East Asia constituting the southern half of the Korean Peninsula. With 52 million people and the world's thirteenth-largest economy by GDP, South Korea is one of the 20th century's most remarkable development success stories — transforming from a war-destroyed agrarian economy in 1953 to a high-income technological powerhouse in 50 years.

The Korean Peninsula has a continuous civilization history of over 2,000 years, with the Three Kingdoms period (57 BCE – 668 CE), the Goryeo dynasty (918–1392), and the Joseon dynasty (1392–1897) shaping Korean culture, Buddhism, Confucianism, and the Korean language and script (hangul, invented 1443). Japanese colonial occupation (1910–1945) and the Korean War (1950–1953) — which killed 2–3 million people — established the division of the peninsula along the 38th parallel. The Republic of Korea was founded under US occupation in 1948.

South Korea's 'Miracle on the Han River' — GDP growth averaging 8% per year from the 1960s through the 1990s under directed state capitalism — was led by chaebols (family conglomerates) like Samsung, Hyundai, and LG. Military dictatorship (1960–1987) was replaced by democracy after the June Struggle (1987). South Korea is now a global leader in semiconductors (Samsung, SK Hynix), shipbuilding, automobiles, and increasingly in cultural exports — K-pop (BTS), K-drama, and Korean cinema (Parasite, 2019 Palme d'Or and Best Picture Oscar).
